# Upstream drift preview — what the NEXT re-pin would hit (forward)

Generated 2026-11-14 by unit DRIFTNEXT, per ADR-0009's re-open protocol
(docs/decisions/0009-tsx-render-path-and-template-engine-parking.md). The
baseline (docs/compat/upstream-drift-baseline.md) mapped the ten commits
BEFORE the pin as the tool's worked example; this file is the FORWARD
counterpart: a preview of the drift a future re-pin of the vendored `gitea/`
submodule would impose on OUR landed pages, services, and tests. It is
produced from real upstream commits, but **it is the map, not the verdict** —
see "The hours question" below.

## How this was produced (regeneration)

- The submodule pin is `fc4936884584a41931906553d96c2601d750e6ef` and the
  working tree was **not moved**: the only submodule operation was a FETCH —
  `git -C gitea fetch origin --no-tags` — never checkout/merge/rebase/reset.
  After the fetch, `git -C gitea rev-parse HEAD` still returned
  `fc49368845…` and `git -C gitea status --porcelain` was empty. (The
  literal `--tags=no` spelled in the tasking is not valid git syntax for this
  version; `--no-tags` is the same intent.)
- Remote state at generation time: `origin/main` = `e2f451ae119b624756143df8
  bd6be6da5858d323` (2026-11-14). Window pin → origin/main: **196 commits**,
  2026-10-24 → 2026-11-14.
- **Tag topology (honest note)**: no tag is a strict DAG-descendant of the
  pin. `v29.0.0-dev` predates the pin entirely, and the `v28.x` release tags
  live on the divergent `release/v28` branch (backports not on main's line —
  the pin is NOT their ancestor). So the "nearest tag" form of the bounded
  cut is impossible and the **N=50 commits** fallback was used: the 50th
  commit after the pin is `405ba258a84a567f230e78f957aeb7014faa2d4b`
  (2026-10-31).
- Analyzer: `scripts/upstream-drift.mjs` (see
  scripts/upstream-drift.README.md). Both runs are FORWARD — `--from` is the
  submodule HEAD, so the tool auto-selected **cite side = from**: every cite
  in our tree is valid at the FROM endpoint and the "moved" verdicts report
  where the cited content sits in the NEW upstream.

Exact regeneration commands:

```bash
git -C gitea fetch origin --no-tags        # fetch-only; the working tree never moves
node scripts/upstream-drift.mjs --from fc49368845 --to 405ba258a84a   # bounded next-minor cut (50 commits)
node scripts/upstream-drift.mjs --from fc49368845 --to e2f451ae11     # full gap (196 commits)
```

Reproducibility (verified 2026-11-14, honestly): for a frozen tree the
analyzer is fully deterministic — same-day reruns are byte-identical (the
only content-independent line in the output is the Generated date). This
verification WAS run: both windows were regenerated a few minutes after the
first pass and the reruns differed ONLY in rows citing the two our-files
then under concurrent sibling edit (`src/api/pulls.test.ts`,
`src/api/routes/pulls.ts` — both dirty in the working tree at generation
time) plus the summary index line they feed. Consequences recorded here:

- The two embedded reports are snapshots taken minutes apart and straddle a
  sibling edit: their citation-index headers read 27,820 vs 27,823 cite
  sites. Each report is internally consistent with its own snapshot.
- Rerunning while sibling agents edit `apps/worker/src` drifts the same way
  — rows citing the live-edited files only. The upstream side of the
  analysis (diff endpoints, hunk parsing, bucket classification) is
  unaffected: it depends only on the two commits named in the command.

Both reports follow verbatim, bounded cut first (nearest-step picture), full
gap second (full-gap picture). The tool's own per-bucket reading guide is in
each report and in the baseline preamble.

## Executive summary

Two windows over the same citation index (~27.8k cite sites in 1,018 of our
files at the pin; the two embedded snapshots straddle a sibling edit and
read 27,820 vs 27,823 — see the reproducibility note above):

| Window | Commits | Upstream files touched | (a) MOVED | (b) REGION CHANGED | (c) FILE ADD/REM | Uncited surface | Our files affected | Tests in scope |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fc49368845` → `405ba258a84a` | 50 (~1 wk) | 368 (342 mod, 18 add, 8 del) | 5,199 sites / 628 files | 646 sites / 198 files | 26 (18 add / 8 del) | 207 | 751 | 657 |
| `fc49368845` → `e2f451ae11` | 196 (~3 wk) | 761 (690 mod, 45 add, 26 del) | 7,519 sites / 745 files | 2,319 sites / 487 files | 71 (45 add / 26 del) | 354 | 875 | 763 |

Read the pair as: even one nominal week of upstream drift touches over 500
of our cite sites, but the (a):(b) ratio (~8:1 in the bounded window, ~3.2:1
in the full window) says most of that mass is mechanical line refreshes; the
behavior re-derivation burden (b) grows faster than linearly with window
length (646 → 2,319 sites for ~4x the commits — sublinear here, but the
full window's extra 146 commits more than tripled it).

The 10 our-files most affected (rows in buckets a+b, full-gap window;
bounded-window rank in parentheses):

1. `src/ui/index.ts` — 1,129 (953) — the ui shell is extremely cite-dense
   (~10k lines); its mass is bucket-(a) refresh work, not 1,129 separate
   behavior questions.
2. `src/services/actions/trigger.ts` — 132 (56)
3. `src/db/schema.ts` — 130 (63)
4. `src/api/services/repository.ts` — 113 (65)
5. `src/api/routes/packages-protocols.ts` — 113 (n/a)
6. `src/api/routes/repo-actions.ts` — 112 (87)
7. `src/services/webhooks-push.ts` — 107 (n/a)
8. `src/api/routes/admin-t2.ts` — 81 (69)
9. `src/ui/session.ts` — 79 (n/a)
10. `src/ui/pages/pull-merge-box.tsx` — 79 (n/a)

(`n/a` = not in the bounded window's top 10; bounded top-10 also includes
`src/services/mail/notify.ts` 82, `src/ui/pages/repo-actions-runs.tsx` 68,
`src/api/services/releases.ts` 68, `src/ui/pages/admin-user-edit.tsx` 57.)

Suites in scope (name-stem match, full-gap window): **763 test files** (657
in the bounded window). Largest families per the census-board hints: tests
under `src/ui/pages` (127 files with affected cites), `src/api/routes`
modules (64) + their tests (57), `src/api/services` modules (46) + tests
(16), `src/ui/__tests__` (35), `src/services/packages` (30), `src/api`
tests (25), `src/services/actions` modules (20) + tests (15).

Bucket (c) highlights (full window): removed upstream surface includes the
openid family (`routers/web/auth/openid.go`, user-setting security openid
pages + tests, `models/user/openid.go`) and `routers/api/v1/admin/adopt.go`;
new surface includes `routers/api/v1/repo/code_search.go`,
`routers/api/packages/terraform_module/`, and `models/issues/code_owner.go`
— port-scope review items, zero dead cites among the removed files so far.

**The hours question (ADR-0009)**: the five-category hours protocol — (i)
pure template-structure sync, (ii) ViewModel adaptation, (iii)
helpers/locals, (iv) permission/behavior changes, (v) test/golden repair —
gets collected with ACTUAL hours WHEN a re-pin actually happens, per
re-pin. This preview deliberately contains no hours estimates: it establishes
the shape of the work (which files, which suites, which buckets) so the
first real re-pin can measure against a known map, not guess from scratch.
The ~50% category-(i) trigger and the POC gates fire on that recorded data,
not on this document.
